newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt miller to revamp five mills by 1998.
newsitem.headline: Egypt miller to revamp five mills by 1998.

text.p: Partly-private North Cairo Flour Mills will update the grinding technique of five mills by the end of 1998 to improve overall productivity, the firm's chairman said in remarks published on Monday.
Chairman Mohammed Khalil also said the miller managed to increase its flour sales and production and that the firm still controlled 32 percent of the market.
Khalil's comments were published in both al-Akhbar and al-Gomhuria goverment newspapers.
He said the five mills to be revamped were the last ones among the firm's total 14 mills that still used stone grinders.

North Cairo was the first milling firm privatised by the state. The authoritative economic weekly al-Borsa said unaudited pre-tax profits for the first eight months of financial 1996/7 year were down to 78.013 million pounds from 82.839 million in same period in the previous year.
Revenues were 608.37 million pounds from 546.79 in the same year ago period, the weekly said. The year begins on July 1.
The Egyptian stock exchange was closed on Sunday and Monday for a public holiday. North Cairo shares last traded on Thursday at 191 pounds.
